tldr: Only the score-marginal median contrast is monotone Lipschitz; both adjusted arm medians may retain a rough common score graph. The complete-class finite-sample risk brackets and partial phase implications are proved nonsharp information, with sharp supplied-propensity order \(n^{-2/3}\) for \(s\ge1/5\) and sharp unknown-propensity order \(n^{-2/3}\) for \(s\ge d/4\). The flat-center diagnostic has that sharp order for every \(s>0\). The explicit witness violates the published individual-arm \(C^2\) condition for every \(0<s\le1\): its roots are non-Lipschitz for \(s<1\) and Lipschitz but nondifferentiable at \(s=1\). The remaining questions are sharp rough-graph coefficient control, a matching original-law modulus, and the complete frontier, including equality logarithms and the exact value of supplying propensity. Wu, Li and Shepherd provide a discrete-stratum consumer for prospective continuous-score calibration benchmarking; their HIV records are not asserted to satisfy this controlled density class.
gap: Zhou, Guo and Zhu supply a propensity-only partial-quantile oracle under individually twice continuously differentiable arm roots. Leqi and Kennedy give target-sensitive median learning against an oracle supplying medians and root densities as well as propensity. Neither retrieved theorem evaluates integrated predictive minimax risk when only the score-marginal contrast is Lipschitz; the explicit common-cusp witness violates the published smooth-arm-root condition. The global positive \(C^3\) density ball is a maintained benchmark, not a published assumption credited to these donors.
fill: The paired-profile coefficient and normalized original-law mixture handles target explicit risk orders and the same-class oracle-survival set. The supplied-propensity lower anchor \(\max\{n^{-2/3},n^{-8s/(6s+1)}\}\), its matched \(s\ge1/5\) upper regime, and the lawful full-confounder lower anchor \(\max\{n^{-2/3},n^{-8s/(4s+d+\min\{2s,1\})}\}\) constrain the answer as to-prove claims. Unmatched branches, the supplied-propensity transition within \([1/6,1/5]\), the candidate survival equality \(8s=d+\min\{2s,1\}\) in the ordinary supplied-propensity branch, and every sharp equality logarithm remain open obligations.
